spec: Plan comparison table: 244 to 320px label column plus equal plan columns, 53 to 66px rows, 1px hairlines at 8% ink, 14px text. Header sticks under the nav and repeats plan, price and a small button per column. Mix ticks, dashes and short real values. Put a toggle or search in the corner cell.

Plan comparison split by 1px vertical hairlines only, no row rules. Rows pitch at 48px, 15px muted labels, 20px filled ink check circles, and a blank cell means no. Groups are 22px bold headings with a collapse chevron, and the rules break at each group. Calm for long feature lists with few text values.

Long comparison table with no rule between rows. One 1px hairline falls only between groups. Group titles 14px/500 in ink, children 14px/400 in muted ink, on about a 48px pitch, with 16px info icons trailing labels. Spacing alone carries the eye across columns, so it stays quiet at 80 or more rows.

Dark comparison matrix: 1px white rules at 6% on both axes, 230px label column, 70px rows, white ticks, and absence shown as a 5px grey dot, never a cross. 8px solid bands in a lifted tone split the groups, and column heads are 20px/600. Nothing reads as a failure.

Developer comparison in one bordered frame: tinted header with logo per column, mono caps group rows, 73px rows holding a 15px name and 13px note with inline code. 28px tinted status circles show yes, partial and no. Capped by a pill that shows the remaining rows, so the page stays short.

Compare hidden until asked for: sticky plan-name row with an 'Expand all' pill, then ten or so 53px category rows, each a 20px icon, 17px name and chevron on a 1px rule. Hover blackens one rule. Opening a row reveals its matrix. Use when the full table would run past 100 rows.

Comparison split by category tabs, because no reader needs every feature. A scrolling pill strip picks one product area, then a table of up to six 164px columns with right-aligned values, small ticks and crosses, a tinted group row and dotted rules inset per cell so column edges stay readable.

Comparison with one plan's column lifted by a full-height tone step: a 2 to 10% fill or side hairlines, 50 to 73px rows, header and cells in the same tint. Pair small multiplier pills on real values. No slab, no shadow. The tint must run unbroken from header to foot.

Own product against rivals: one solid accent column about 204px wide overshooting the rows by 30 to 40px top and bottom, white ring checks inside, rival column with pale crosses, 75px rows, row rules passing behind the slab. Works with two to three columns and ten rows at most.

Small rate table inside a dark feature cell: 1px grid, 48px rows, rivals in 12px grey. Your own row alone gets an accent frame, a dark tint of that accent, your logo and the winning number in full accent. Everything else stays grey, so the eye needs no reading.

Two columns or panels, no grid: 'before' muted with crosses or every line struck through, 'after' at full contrast with ticks or a keyline. 24px gap, 16 to 18px lines. Strikethrough does the disqualifying. Works as a qualifier too: who this is for, and who it is not for.

Cost difference shown as length: rival a full-width bar with its price, yours a 12px dot or a short bar. 12 to 32px bar height, 22px tabular prices right-aligned, a row of shared assumptions above and small-print method below. Use only with honest, sourced numbers.

Product pricing as a white card with rows: name and short description left, a tinted rate cell right, split by 1px dashed lines, 8px radius, soft shadow. Headline rate 16 to 18px, conditions 13px beneath. Reads like a bank's fee schedule. Right for usage fees that need sentences, not ticks.

Three to four equal cards compare approaches or formats: 10 to 12px radius, title 16px/600, facts in grey rows, the recommended card tinted. Simple and safe for consumer and education pages. Use when options differ in kind rather than feature by feature; avoid when a real table would be clearer.

A plain documentation table: 1px pale grid on every cell, tinted header, 14px bold, 27 to 48px rows, optional zebra, keyboard chips or short values. No plan marketing at all. Correct for specs, shortcuts, fees and lens options, where scanning a fact matters more than any impression.

A plain list replaces the table: tinted panel radius 28, centred 48px heading, then three text columns of 17/21 muted names, with small chevrons on those that link. For answering 'does it work with mine?' when the answer is a list of devices or models.

Three or four plans in one frame sharing 1px rules, no gaps, radius 0 to 8. 32px padding, 14px name, 48 to 56px price, muted one-line fit, then 'Everything in X, plus' list. Recommended cell is one tone brighter, with the only filled button. Use subgrid so rows align across plans.

Three to five separate plan cards, 1px line, no fill or a faint one, no shadow, gap 16 to 32, radius 4 to 24. 24 to 32px padding: name, 30 to 36px price, one-line fit, full-width button, then six to eight ticks at 30 to 36px pitch. Pick the recommended plan with a small tag.

Plan cards one tone step off the page, no border or shadow, or a 5% hairline, gap 8 to 10, radius 4 to 16, 16 to 24px padding. Every button is a grey pill except the recommended plan's, which is solid ink, so one filled button makes the choice. Feature lists grouped under small rules.

Four plan cards, 16px gap, 14px radius, 1px hairlines, with exactly one filled solid ink and its button flipped to white. Keep type and structure identical across cards. The inversion is the recommendation, so drop badges. Keep inverted on phones. Works from three to four plans.

Plans sit in one shell and the recommended column rises 16 to 32px above and below its neighbours, with a lighter fill or a 2px outline and a slightly larger title. No drop shadow is needed, because the broken top edge does the lifting. Three to five columns.

Featured plan gets no lift, no border, no badge. Only colour marks it: an accent mono label, a white filled pill where others are outlined, accent square bullets, brighter text. Other plans stay in grey. Quietest way to recommend, and strongest on dark ruled grids.

Pricing built as a product window: shell radius 16, padding 4, 44px title row, then four panes radius 12 in a lifted dark tone with 4px gutters. 20px name with muted audience note right, 30px price, one fee row, hairline, ticks pinned to the base. No per-plan button, no featured plan.

One 1024px sheet, 12px radius, soft shadow, holds all plans. Top strip carries a caps title and annual toggle, then three columns split by hairlines, then a tinted bottom strip with an upsell line. Plans read as a single document rather than competing cards.

Each plan column opens with a distinct tile, about 262 by 200px at radius 12 to 16, holding name and price or a mascot, art or black header block. Button under the tile, feature list open beneath it on the page with no card. One tile may carry a grain gradient to mark the pick.

One offer in one wide card, about 1088 by 426, radius 24, 1px warm line, soft tinted shadow. Left: small label, 40px name, 80px price with small unit, muted billing line, 50px full-width button. 1px vertical rule. Right: seven to nine ticks at 36px pitch.

One plan as a 416px card under a Yearly/Monthly pill: 16px item left, dotted leader, right-aligned 13px mono caps status, either included or a dated promise. Full-width 48px button below. Reads like a receipt, so the honest 'coming soon' line builds trust.

One price set as a sentence or a large figure with no plan grid: centred or left, 48 to 80px figure with small unit and the conditions at text size, a link or button below. For one product, one fee, a quote-based service or a set menu.

Two plan cards side by side, radius 10 to 20: a quiet free or basic card next to a filled or tinted paid card. Same bullet structure in both, 24 to 45px price, full-width button. Emphasis comes from fill and button alone. Use when only two offers exist.

Two 532 by 287 cards, 16px gap, 8px radius. Standard card: copy left, tinted rate panel right inset 4px. Custom card in dark ink: copy left, four stacked chips right inset 4px. Separates pay-as-you-go from talk-to-us without a tier table.

Prices as list rows, not cards: 14 to 15px label left, right-aligned bold price, 28 to 75px pitch, hairlines or none, inside the text column. Suits museum admission, service fees, or a small product's plans. Add a foot row linking to details. Tabular numerals, no icons.

Price set by the reader: slider with 1M, 10M and 50M ticks or an inline select per plan, boxed value, per-unit rate, and a bar reading 'Estimated total' with a button. Prices update live with no layout shift. For metered products where a flat tier table would mislead.

White or lifted plan cards on a saturated field or dark colour band, radius 16 to 24, 22px gaps, no highlighted tier needed because the field already gives the section its energy. Keep one colour plus white. Works for bold consumer and developer brands; avoid behind dense lists.

Plans as link tiles rather than tables: 24px radius, 24px padding, 24px name, 18px price, 16px muted line, one arrow bottom right, whole tile clickable. Three over two on a dark ground. For consumer accounts or packages where comparison happens on the next page.

Price as the hero object: four split-flap tiles about 200 by 128, radius 16, subtle dark gradient, thin numerals crossing an 8px split, flipping when a large text toggle switches monthly to yearly. One striking moment for a one-price product, never for a tier table.

FAQ as one reading column, 640 to 944px, centred or left aligned, heading aligned to it. Rows pitch 57 to 88px on 1px hairlines, 16px/500 to 600 questions, thin plus or chevron at far right, no cards, all collapsed. Answers 16px at 1.6 in muted ink, under 34em.

FAQ with heading alone in the left column and rows in the right half: 36 to 52px title top left, 56 to 75px rows, 1px rules top and bottom, 16 to 20px questions, 16px chevrons. Optional tone band behind. The empty left column gives a dull section its composure.

Split FAQ with one line drawing, photo or mascot under the title in the left column, 44 to 55px heading, rows right at 656px, 74px pitch, plus at right. A section band in brand colour is common. Art must belong to the brand, or leave the column empty.

FAQ rows as tone tiles, no rules: 56 to 80px tall, 8 to 12px gaps, radius 8 to 22, 16 to 20px question, thin plus or a 36px white disc holding a chevron. Open row expands within its own fill. Title left. A final 'Ask anything else' row can route to a person.

FAQ rows as outlined boxes: 1px line, radius 0 to 16, 58 to 120px tall, 12 to 24px gaps. A square toggle button at right, 36 to 44px, gives it a form-like, deliberate feel. Heavier than rules, so match it to a square, printed or industrial page.

FAQ numbered like an index: right-hand list about 52% wide, 68px rows, no dividers, grey 20px tabular index, 20px question, tiny chevron. Hover fills the whole row one tone at radius 6. Numbers state the length honestly and help on a sales call.

Questions set as large as section headings: 24 to 40px, 80 to 135px rows, 1px rules, thin plus or a filled disc. Hover or open fills the row or turns the type to accent. Makes a few FAQs read as statements. Six to ten short questions at most.

FAQ with a heavy control as the only strong object: 40px solid ink discs holding a thin white plus, 88px rows, 20px/600 questions, 1px rules, a heading row with a 56px button right. Controls that bold suit a soft page that needs a firm ending.

Rows with no visible dividers that come alive on hover: the hovered row lifts into a soft panel at radius 25, or fills one tone step across the full 1300px width. 20px questions at 61 to 112px pitch. Depends on hover, so keep a clear chevron for touch.

No accordion. Every answer open in a 670px left-aligned column: 22px display questions, 16/26 body, 34px between pairs, real links, a 20px hash anchor appearing in the left margin on hover. Searchable with cmd-F and linkable. Needs answers worth reading and suits developer tools.

Master and detail: question list left, one answer pane right. Active row lighter, pane echoes the question and answers in a chat bubble or sand panel with small pagination. Shell radius 32 with 16px inset panes. Eight questions at most. Needs a stacked accordion on phones.

Long FAQs split by topic: a left rail of 24px category names beside 853px rows at 81px pitch, or tabs above a 640px column, or two audience-named columns. Each group keeps the same row. Answers 'which part applies to me' before anyone reads a question.

Two 610px columns of 44 to 48px rows, 16px/700 questions, 12px chevrons, ten questions visible at once. No panels or shading. Compact, for a FAQ that must not take a whole screen. Answers push only their own column, so keep them short.

Dense disclosure rows for details, not persuasion: 40 to 48px tall, 14px labels, 1px rules, plus or chevron at right. Use under a product buy box, on visit pages, or for 17 or more questions where density signals candour. Upper-case or mono labels suit stores.

The whole FAQ sits in one tinted or white sheet, 710 to 900px, radius 10 to 16, 48px padding, 70px rows on hairlines, chevrons in 24px discs that darken when open. Reads as a reference area. Use it when the page behind is busy or dark.

FAQ and final ask share one screen: left column 64/64 closing heading and pill, right a 498px stack of 60px rows, radius 8, 12px gap. Saves a section on short pages and keeps the button beside the last doubt it answers.

Page ends on its own ground: no panel, gradient or image, 130 to 230px padding above and below. Centred 48 to 72px two-line sentence, tight leading, one filled and one quiet 44px pill, 12px apart. The only centred block on a left-aligned page, so the change of axis signals the end.

No band or fill. Heading left, 36 to 56px over two lines, with one sentence and a 48px button in a right column, or the buttons alone on the same line. Under a hairline, about 120px padding. Confidence comes from size. Suits calm finance and SaaS pages.

Close framed by the page's rails: a 190 to 415px band between two full-bleed hairlines, no colour change, where side rails stop. 34 to 64px line left or centred, two 42 to 44px pills. Needs a visible rule system earlier on the page, or it reads as empty.

The button is the design: centred 64 to 80px headline, muted line, then a 64 to 72px button, radius 18 to 20, 24 to 32px bold label, or a giant 750px pill holding the whole line. Add ratings or a checklist beneath. Say one thing.

The end rhymes with the start: repeat the hero mark, panel, icon shape or slogan at a new scale. A 590px faded squircle echoing the app icon, a ghost logo bleeding off a corner, or the hero stack again. Quiet, and needs no new art.

Inset panel one tone off the page, radius 6 to 42, 24 to 32px page inset, 320 to 460px tall. 48 to 52px heading left or centred, filled and outlined buttons. Optional blurred bloom in two hues on the right half, kept pale, never behind the text.

One inset panel in full brand colour or dark ink, 1248 to 1376px, radius 12 to 20, 48 to 72px heading, two buttons. It works only if it is the one saturated surface on the page. Add one owned detail: a drawn line, a notch, a pattern.

Tinted inset panel, about 282 to 450px tall, radius 24, carrying a brand pattern with the centre cleared for text: 1px rings radiating from the button, pixel blocks at both sides, contour lines. 32 to 64px heading. The pattern rewards attention without competing with it.

Full-bleed colour band, 230 to 540px, centred 40 to 56px heading, 96px padding, one or two 48px buttons. Plain and common, the fallback of template pages. Lift it with a two-tone heading or a flat line drawing, and let it butt onto the footer.

Dark or white field with soft colour pooled at its edges: glows high behind a centred app icon, or blooms in the bottom corners, 40 to 64px heading on clean ground, one 48px button. Text never sits on the brightest area. Flows into the footer without a seam.

Closing on a real photograph or film: full bleed or a 1376px card at radius 32, 48 to 120px white heading placed in the image's own shadow, 16 to 22px copy, one white pill. Use a local scrim. Repeat the hero's world so the page closes a loop.

Half photo, half flat panel: 1360 by 450, radius 8 to 24, warm image beside a 48px heading, small eyebrow and a full-width 48px button pinned to the base. Or a 270px flush photo on the right of a dark card. Safe for health, retail and culture.

A 540px left-aligned card of dark grain lit from one side, radius 12, white mark, 36/39 heading, small white button. The right half of the row stays empty, so the close reads as a placed object rather than a band. Sits just above a matching dark footer.

Display type carries the ending: 100 to 250px flush left, leading under 1, a last word in accent or underlined, install block or field small beside it. On a black band or field. Keep a sharp scale contrast with something tiny next to it.

The close is a stack of links, not a band. Up to 110px lines filling the width, each with a thin chevron flush right, or 52px bar buttons with mono caps, or a 68px strip of numbered links. Navigation becomes type. Use when several next steps are equal.

End by routing, not by shouting: heading left, then two or three cards or rows, one per next step, each with title, one line and a 44 to 60px arrow disc. Radius 12 on a tinted panel at radius 24. Two-audience pages use two equal columns.

The last call to action is the product: centred 48px heading, then a real 54 to 62px input, up to 766px wide, radius 14, with its action inside. Prompt box, URL field, file drop or preset amounts. Starts the first task instead of describing it.

The close is the download itself: OS columns of chips split by 1px rules, a copyable install command beside a docs button, or a QR card with store ratings for desktop visitors. Real commands, real platforms. Nothing to read, one thing to do.

Heading and buttons left, a working piece of the product right: a status stack, a fan of app screens, devices on a reflective floor, an editor crop flush to the edge. Clipped by the panel. Must be current product, not a stock mock.

The close physically joins the footer: the page plate, inset 52px from one side, ends in a 50px corner and reveals colour beneath, or a white card straddles the seam, or the footer overlaps a grain band. Depth with no shadow, and the page reads as one object.

Centred 48 to 64px heading in a clear middle, ringed by scattered objects: 68px logo tiles, framed photos at differing sizes, pixel sprites. A grainy glow rising through the lower third can tint the ones it touches. Objects must be real integrations, products or people.

Personality closes the page: a mascot rising from the panel's edge, a full cast lined up on the footer, a straight-faced parody of sales tactics that still converts. 60px heading, one button. Only for brands already that voice. Never on health, law or finance.

One owned drawing fills half the band: extruded ribbons, a dithered ASCII tree, a chrome wordmark, overlapping lens circles, tilted slab. Heading and pill on the other side. It must be made for this brand and appear earlier on the page, or it reads as decoration.

The contact detail is the headline: a 48px phone number on a 90px strip, or a 76px email address in the page's display type, with no button. For agencies, local trades and voice products, where one action really is a call or an email.

A 60 to 66px bar docked to the viewport base with 8px inset: 14px bold label, price or avatar stack, one 48px pill. Stays through all scrolling. Use for one strong consumer offer, never with a chat bubble or cookie bar competing for the same edge.

Email field as a single line: 1 to 1.5px underline, 12 to 16px placeholder, submit as plain text at the far end of the same line or a small block abutting it, 11px consent below. No box. 360 to 580px wide. Works on photos and dark blocks.

Sign-up as one ruled row across the page: a 32px sentence on a 2px rule, 908px wide, then 20px on, a 444px email field sitting on the same rule, with plain Submit text at the right. No box and no button. Reads as a line in a magazine.

Heading, one line of copy, then a 40 to 48px field and a separate button side by side, 8 to 12px apart, 385 to 540px total, often centred. Correct and invisible. Lift it with a line of real proof or a joke in the copy.

Button lives inside the field: 50 to 62px capsule or 52px square outline, inset 4 to 8px, 16px placeholder, button or arrow seated inside. Button height equals field height minus twice the inset, and inner radius equals outer minus inset. Reads as one object.

Email field as a flat tone with no border, radius or visible button: 30 to 60px tall, grey fill two to four steps off the page, small caps placeholder. Suits fashion, galleries and luxury. Keep a keyboard submit and a visible label.

The field is the section: 64 to 67px tall, up to 683px wide, 42px placeholder or a mono placeholder that keeps the developer voice, submit at right or a 64px button beside it, on a grey or flat colour band.

No field on the page: a label, one sentence and a Subscribe pill or text link, about 120px tall, following the page grid like any other section. Or one huge staggered link. Sign-up moves to its own page, so the page stays in its own voice.

Row inside the footer between two 1px rules at 8%: 20/600 title and 15px line left, 48px outlined input about 330px wide plus button right, 13px consent below. Button stays grey until the field has content. Quiet, and always reachable.

Sign-up on a photograph: full-bleed band or a card at radius 32 with 7px margin, 44px headline, 62px white field, 48px pill, on the calm side of a warm portrait. Check text against the busiest pixel; a busy image defeats it.

Half real photograph, half flat panel in brand colour: heading, one line, email field and button. Bands 260 to 400px tall. Good for food, culture and hospitality, where the picture is the reason to subscribe.

Full-width flat colour band with a sign-up heading left and small free-text copy right, little else. Works as a page-level colour moment for a culture listing or daily product. Keep to one colour and white.

An owned illustration gives the sign-up a character: a pixel mascot in an envelope, a spot drawing on a pale panel, art dissolving into the form's ground. 32 to 36px bold heading, a caption saying how often it arrives, underline or 42px input. The drawing is the reason to look.

Centred 54px heading and 50px input, with product renders floating around: sharp near the top, one large and blurred in front for depth, or a generated torn shape behind. Peach or brand gradient rising from one corner. Needs real rendered objects.

Centred 440 to 600px modal over a dimmed page, half lifestyle photo, half form with a discount headline, one field, black button and an underlined decline link. It interrupts on arrival, so delay it, offer real value and keep close obvious. Stores only.

Persistent small cue instead of a modal: a 40 by 240px rotated tab on the right edge, a 214 by 48px corner tab, or a 60px bottom bar with a close x. Never covers a photo's subject and stays reachable.

Small card holding the sign-up inside a grid or sidebar: 300 to 500px, 12 to 24px radius, title, one line, field or button, sitting in the same slot as a quote or article. Joins the page's rhythm instead of interrupting it.

Two fields stacked in one container: 460px wide, radius 24, 2px spectral or thin outline, 13px labels above 18px placeholders, split by a hairline, then a full-width 52px pill. For private betas and waitlists, where asking a role is worth it.

Sales contact split: left 64px headline, 18px muted line, then logos with one stat each. Right 568px form on the bare page: 14/500 labels, 38px inputs, radius 6, 1px line, 2-up rows at 16px gap, 26px between groups, 150px textarea, pill submit, 12px consent. Proof sits beside the ask.

Fields are single lines: 1px bottom rule, 12px labels above or inside, 16px light values, 56px or more between rows, 2-up on desktop. A large 60 to 90px title left. Rule turns full ink on focus. Pill or block submit. For studios, hospitality and portfolios.

Form in one tinted panel, 8px radius, 24px padding: 16/600 labels with muted asterisks, 42px white square-cornered inputs, 1px grey line, 16px gutters, 42px dark button bottom left with an arrow. Or a slate panel with a neon submit. Reads as one task.

Long form split into steps: a 540 to 608px card or column, two to four fields per step, 'Step 1 of 2' caption or numbered tabs, full-width 46px Next. First step asks only email and one qualifier. Filled 58px fields with labels inside, or inline labels.

Contact as a conversation: a phone-like sheet with a handle and avatar, one question at a time in 16px, ghost answer, circular arrow. Email address with a Copy pill beside it for people who prefer to write. For agencies and AI products.

The form is replaced by a calendar: 874px white scheduler radius 8 with host and agenda pane, month grid and time buttons, on a full-bleed brand colour under a 60px centred headline. One step closer to the meeting than a message.

Dark or coloured band: left 48 to 64px headline, 18px copy, three tick lines saying what happens next. Right a 517px white card, radius 16 to 28, 46px inputs, 50px accent submit. An offset colour slab behind the card can give it weight.

Form card placed over a 3D scene, photo or blurred image: 330 to 500px, radius 8 to 20, small labels, stacked fields. Legible only with a solid or strong frosted card. Works when the art is the brand and the form short.

No form: a sentence with two underlined links, big labelled emails, a phone number, or offices beside a photograph. For portfolios, studios, restaurants and dentists, where a human answers and the fastest route is a call or an email.

Before any field, route the visitor: 48px heading left, right column of four rows on near-ink 1px rules, each a 22px title with arrow and a 14px line. Mono links below the heading for the rest. Sends sales, support and partners to different places.

Default stacked form: 44px white fields, radius 4, 1px line, 12px labels above, a dropdown, a checkbox, a dark button. Correct and anonymous. Use it for institutions, and spend effort on field count, error text and what happens next.

For a physical place, contact is directions: a map with brand-coloured pins beside a colour panel with a 51px 'Directions' heading, a journey-planner button and collapsible rows for tube, bus and parking on underline rules.
